title: No charges for Mountie in God's Lake shooting
article: No criminal charges will be laid against an RCMP officer who shot and killed a man on a northern Manitoba First Nation last year.
Paul Leonard Duck, 52, was fatally shot early in the morning of March 15, 2011, on the God's Lake First Nation.

An independent probe by the Saskatoon Police Service, along with an Ontario Crown review of the case, found no evidence to warrant criminal charges in the shooting, Saskatoon police announced Wednesday.
The investigation found that two RCMP officers were guarding the scene of a house fire at around 1:35 a.m. CT, when they were confronted by an armed man.
One of the Mounties shot the man twice.
An autopsy found that Duck died from those wounds, according to Saskatoon police.
Members of Duck's family have said he fired a shotgun in the air, in an attempt to break up a dispute between two groups of teenagers, before running to the RCMP officers to get help.

It is RCMP policy in Manitoba to ask an external agency to investigate serious cases involving RCMP members. A senior member of the Saskatoon force conducted the probe, with help from the RCMP's serious crimes unit.
An inquest into Duck's death is still pending.
